raw.assessment: The incumbent supports the required CSV workflow and appears useful under stable assignments: those 24 files had seven-minute median handling. Overall course-set accuracy was 80%, below 95%, and handling was 17 minutes, above 12. Assignment changes occurred in six affected exports, supporting investigation of temporal selection without establishing causation. The two renamed-course cases limit an assignment-only account: selection or human recognition could also fail. Zero observed cross-center rows is limited evidence because the split-course center was absent. Fast execution and slow replacement delivery suggest a separate service delay, not necessarily the source of measured handling time.

openings.claim: Current assignment or course-name interpretation may diverge from the intended historical week, while stable cases remain easy to use.
openings.delta: Distinguish incorrect export membership from correct membership that coordinators cannot recognize after a rename.
openings.prediction: With an agreed intended course set held fixed, changing only current assignment or display name will either change exported membership or change coordinator recognition despite identical membership.
openings.probe: Use fabricated staging cases for midweek reassignment and rename. Compare exported membership before and after each change, then ask consenting coordinators to identify included courses. Treat disagreement over the intended set as unresolved timetable semantics.
assumptions: Staging can reproduce the relevant selection behavior.
Existing identifiers or fabricated fixtures allow membership comparison without altering the documented CSV schema.

openings.claim: Does excess active handling arise mainly from course checking and correction, replacement requests, or spreadsheet importing?
openings.delta: Separate coordinator effort from replacement elapsed time before selecting the bounded intervention.
openings.prediction: A replacement-access intervention would reduce median handling only if requesting and following up consumes substantial active time; long passive waits alone would not support that prediction.
openings.probe: In the two short sessions, have six coordinators process fabricated unchanged and changed-course files in authorized workspaces. Time checking, correction, downloading, importing, and requesting separately; record passive waits separately. Use the results to bound a change within six engineer-days and existing hosting.
assumptions: Fabricated tasks approximate ordinary handling sufficiently to prioritize further work.
Sessions require no interruption of live attendance entry or external processing of participant names.

raw.assessment: Assignment changes and renaming are associated with affected exports; neither is a demonstrated cause. Two hypotheses relocate course selection and replacement dispatch into the private service. Neither establishes success across 40 exports; the unsampled course split remains an isolation test case.

openings.claim: Let a private center-and-week manifest perform course selection: the coordinator chooses intended course identities from their authorized list, and the exporter uses that manifest independently of current instructor assignment and display names.
openings.delta: The interface captures intended membership before extraction, replacing repeated comparison of CSV course names with a separate timetable. The exported CSV retains its documented schema.
openings.prediction: If unstable membership selection drives the observed errors, manifest-driven exports retain intended courses through instructor changes and renaming, with less total selection-plus-checking time.
openings.probe: In fabricated staging, compare existing and manifest-driven exports for unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split courses. Six coordinators use predetermined intended sets; measure selection and checking time, omissions and foreign-center rows. Continue attendance entry during export.
assumptions: Usable persistent course identities exist or fit the six-engineer-day limit.
Coordinators can identify intended membership; timetable accuracy remains unmeasured.
Every selected identity is checked against workspace authorization, with private processing, unchanged hosting and no attendance write lock.

openings.claim: Let an authorized workspace control dispatch and deliver replacement exports directly through the existing job runner.
openings.delta: Coordinator action becomes job input and completion becomes an immediately available private download, replacing the intervening request-to-delivery process.
openings.prediction: If dispatch or delivery causes the observed wait, request-to-download delay falls substantially while course-set accuracy may remain unchanged.
openings.probe: Timestamp request, job start, completion and download availability for the existing process and a staged direct control. Separately time active coordinator handling; test duplicate requests, unauthorized centers and concurrent attendance entry.
assumptions: The existing runner can accept authorized bounded requests within six engineer-days without new hosting expenditure.
Deduplicated requests preserve attendance availability, center isolation and the documented CSV schema.
Faster availability may reduce elapsed delay without reducing active handling time.

openings.claim: Distinguish historical membership errors from rename recognition; a private center/week manifest could select intended course identities independently of current assignments and names.
openings.discriminator: Hold intended membership fixed; vary assignment/name, then compare exported membership and coordinator recognition.
openings.fit: Uncertain: requires persistent identities, authorization per identity and affordable implementation.
openings.probe: Compare incumbent/manifest on fabricated unchanged, reassigned, renamed and split courses; measure omissions, foreign rows and total selection/checking effort during concurrent attendance entry.
openings.uncertainty: Association is not causation; timetable correctness, intended-set agreement and coordinator recognition remain unresolved.

openings.claim: Authorized direct dispatch/download through the existing runner could shorten replacement delivery; its handling-time benefit depends on active request/follow-up effort.
openings.discriminator: Separate active checking, correction, requesting, downloading and importing from passive waits.
openings.fit: Uncertain: bounded, deduplicated requests must fit existing hosting and six engineer-days.
openings.probe: Use six coordinators in two short fabricated sessions; compare request/start/completion/download timestamps and active effort; test duplicates, unauthorized centers and concurrent attendance.
openings.uncertainty: Import or checking may dominate; faster delivery may leave accuracy and handling unchanged; fabricated tasks may differ from practice.

post_distill.decision: Diagnose before choosing. Both retain private authorized processing, documented CSV, six-day/hosting limits and uninterrupted attendance. Split-center isolation remains unproven. Validate chosen change across 40 exports: median handling <=12 minutes, intended sets >=95%, zero foreign records.
